clue.text: Small comfort taking in better marine view

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: taking in means the comfort word swallows the better word inside it

parts.note: ease means comfort, as in living a life of ease
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a little consolation from an improved view of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a picture or prospect of the sea, so a marine view describes it exactly.

clue.text: Praise — and for Le Monde: Times almost entirely suppressed

indicators.note: suppressed means held down inside the French conjunction, which encloses the other letters

parts.note: et is the French word for and, as a Paris newspaper would print it
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: almost means the word for entirely loses its final letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A French newspaper keeps its praise quiet while a London rival is nearly silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Le Monde' and 'Times' look like rival newspapers; one supplies French, the other the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to glorify or extol them, a verb synonym for praise.

clue.text: Left during meal, having increased flexibility

indicators.note: during means the letter sits inside the meal word, as if it happens within it

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone left in the middle of dinner and came away more limber.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppler is the comparative of supple, so it describes something that has gained bendiness.

clue.text: Conversion accepted by nobleman after departure of English religious figure

indicators.note: accepted by means the conversion word is taken inside the shortened title
after departure of means the nobleman's title loses the English letter

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
a conversion is a change from one thing to another

explanation.surface: A peer embraces a new faith once the Englishman has left, becoming a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is an angel of high rank in Christian tradition, a figure revered in religion.

clue.text: Eastern sea-creature losing tail is put out

indicators.note: losing tail means the creature's name drops its last letter

parts.note: a manatee is a large plant-eating marine mammal, the sea cow

explanation.surface: An oriental sea cow loses its tail and is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put out' suggests annoyance; here it means is given off or sent forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, so it is what something does when it is put out.

clue.text: Recalled shops as sources of wool

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the shopping word is read backwards

parts.note: a mall is a precinct of shops

explanation.surface: Shops have been withdrawn because they were where the wool came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American animals whose fleece is spun into yarn, so they supply wool.

clue.text: Fix source of ore, including source of gold

indicators.note: including means the vein word holds the picked letter within it

parts.note: a lode is a vein of metal ore in rock

indicators.note: source of picks just the initial letter of the next word, its point of origin

explanation.surface: A miner pins down a vein of ore with a trace of gold in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge something is to fix or embed it firmly, as a bullet lodges in a wall.

clue.text: Religious leader engaged in excellent form of reasoning

indicators.note: engaged in means the monastic head is placed within the excellent pair

parts.note: A1 means first-class or excellent, written here with the letter I for the figure one
a prior is the head of a priory of monks

explanation.surface: A cleric is busy with a first-rate kind of argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from principles or assumptions before experience, a recognised kind of logical argument.

clue.text: A category encompassing marine life initially provides warning

indicators.note: encompassing means the category word surrounds the marine letters

parts.note: a label is a classifying tag or category
RM stands for Royal Marines, so a marine

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A grouping that takes in sea life offers a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm bell is a signal of danger, figuratively any early sign that something is wrong.

clue.text: Mould political response mostly in account

indicators.note: in means the shortened word goes inside the account letters
mostly means the spin word loses its final letter

parts.note: spin is the slanted presentation politicians give to news

explanation.surface: A clerk shapes the party line, more or less, into the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly set in a shaped mould, so the dish is often called a mould.

clue.text: A large college's boss holding room for local dignitary

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: holding means the head's title contains the room letters

parts.note: a dean heads a college or faculty

explanation.surface: The head of a big college keeps a room for a visiting town worthy.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a town or borough council, a civic figure of standing.

clue.text: Computer professionals worried about a point recurring, covering part of Europe

indicators.note: about means the computer letters and the worried word go round the rest

parts.note: IT, information technology, stands for the computer people
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

indicators.note: recurring is read as running back, so the point word is turned round

parts.note: a nail is a pointed pin, and some dictionaries give point as a sense

explanation.surface: IT staff fret over a repeating decimal point that spans a region of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a point recurring' suggests a decimal, but here the point is a pin turned round by 'recurring', and 'about' has the outer pair wrap the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Italianate means in the Italian style, so it relates to a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: Old bad actors not acting, getting quantity of resistance

indicators.note: not means the acting letter is removed from the actors

parts.note: hams are actors who overact
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a job title

explanation.surface: Washed-up overactors who no longer work meet some opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance is measured in units named after the physicist Georg Ohm, so these quantify it.

clue.text: Lass repelled by attention-seeker? That's the drill

parts.note: oi is the shout used to get someone's notice

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the lass word is read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl rebuffed by a show-off shrugs that this is how things go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the drill' sounds like 'that's the routine'; here the drill is literal machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is the structure that bores down to oil, so it is the drilling installation itself.

clue.text: I note special quality: one course served up as starter

parts.note: it means that indefinable special appeal, as in she's got it

indicators.note: served up, in a down answer, means the course and one are written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a rota is a course or rotation of duties
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diner records a special touch: a single dish served as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a menu's first course; it means someone who starts things.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiator is a person who begins or launches something, so a starter in that sense.

clue.text: Brought out sources of European law I quoted

indicators.note: sources of means the opening letters of the following words

parts.note: to cite is to quote, so quoted gives cited

explanation.surface: A lawyer drew out the origins of European law that they quoted.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response or fact, so elicited is brought out.

clue.text: Chosen officer covering a wide area

parts.note: in means elected or chosen, as a party is in
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A selected officer is posted to cover a broad territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means broadly or as a whole, speaking across the full range of cases.

clue.text: Failure to keep back in dodgy bar? Move to another view

indicators.note: in means the reversed word is placed inside the bar word

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar

indicators.note: back means the failure word is read in reverse

parts.note: a loss is a failure or defeat

explanation.surface: A seedy pub's failure leads to someone deciding to go elsewhere for the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' is linking padding here; 'back' turns the failure round before 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In film, a dissolve is a gradual transition fading one scene into the next.

clue.text: Group about to finish cooking utensil

indicators.note: about means the group word goes around the finish word

parts.note: a set is a group of things
to kill is to finish off

explanation.surface: A gang plans to finish off someone with a kitchen implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, a piece of cookware used on the hob.

clue.text: Government computer network installed in the last place in the country

indicators.note: installed in means the government and network letters are fitted inside the end word

parts.note: the end is the final place
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A state network gets set up in the remotest corner of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: England is a country, one of the four nations of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Books involved in storm and chatter

indicators.note: involved in means the books letters are wrapped inside the storm word

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind or storm
B is an abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Books get caught up in a tempest and idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To gabble is to talk rapidly and unintelligibly, a form of chatter.

clue.text: Looked after by South Africa, put in to face the bowling

indicators.note: put in means the by and South Africa letters go inside the batting word

parts.note: in cricket, to bat is to face the bowling

explanation.surface: A cricketer sent in by South Africa to face the bowlers has been minding things.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter faces balls bowled at them, so to face the bowling is to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after a child while the parents are out, so the past tense is looked after.

clue.text: Setter's repeatedly backing opera heroine

indicators.note: backing means the doubled letters are read backwards
repeatedly means the shortened phrase is written twice

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: The setter keeps supporting a favourite operatic leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the doomed seamstress who is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme.

clue.text: Boxing nonsense swamping a good boxing film

indicators.note: swamping means the boxing word engulfs the a and good letters

parts.note: the ring is where boxing takes place, so the sport is the ring
bull is nonsense, short for a coarser word

explanation.surface: A lot of fight talk overwhelms a decent prizefighting movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging Bull is Martin Scorsese's 1980 film about the boxer Jake LaMotta.

clue.text: Repetitive piece of music runs on just the same

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: A repetitive tune goes on and on exactly the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form whose main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Game of chance — fate as well? Not entirely

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

indicators.note: not entirely means the also word loses its final letter

parts.note: too means as well, also

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders whether a game of chance is fate too, or not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game in which numbers are drawn at random, a game ruled by chance.

clue.text: US city home to athletic female sprinter?

indicators.note: home to means the city houses the athletic letter inside it

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of Georgia in the United States
A is an abbreviation for athletic, as in an amateur athletic association

explanation.surface: An American city hosts a speedy woman runner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a sprinter from Greek myth, not a modern athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a huntress famed for her speed, beaten in a footrace only by a trick with golden apples.

clue.text: Lack of activity around one exam

indicators.note: around means the rest word goes round the numeral

parts.note: rest is a lack of activity
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Idleness surrounds a lone student facing an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an examination taken again after failing it the first time.

clue.text: Reached where river enters cave

indicators.note: enters means the river letter goes into the reached phrase

parts.note: got to means reached, as in got to the station

explanation.surface: Explorers arrived at the spot where a stream flows into a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cavern, so it is a kind of cave.

clue.text: Broadening sources of Dutch and Irish, with nothing in classical language

indicators.note: sources of means the first letters of the next two words
in means the nothing letter is put inside the language word

parts.note: Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Dutch and Irish origins broaden with nothing in an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilation is widening or expansion, as when a pupil enlarges, so it is broadening.
